title: Release history
description: Every DocKitty toolkit release, rendered at build time from the repository's CHANGELOG.md.
markdown:
All notable changes to `@spec-kitty/doc-toolkit` are recorded here. The format
follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and the project
adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

### 💥 Breaking

- **`dockitty-assert-plantuml-no-remote-include --service-container` now fails
  service setups it used to pass (#268).** Before, the check passed any
  service that refused its test include. Now, with the opt-in unset, it fails
  when the named container has: a `PLANTUML_SECURITY_PROFILE` that is missing
  or not `SANDBOX`; a security-relevant `-D` property, `plantuml.*` env key or
  `PLANTUML_PROPERTY_FILE`; a Java `@argfile`; or a local `--server` port the
  container does not publish on a matching address. An empty value for any
  flag now exits 2. To fix: set `PLANTUML_SECURITY_PROFILE=SANDBOX` on the
  service (or declare the opt-in), move PlantUML settings into the two
  environment variables, and name the container that serves `--server`. See the
  [0.6 to 0.7 migration guide](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/migrations/0.6-to-0.7.md).

### Added

- **Operators can let PlantUML fetch declared remote includes (#268).** Before,
  every URL include failed the build under the hardened `SANDBOX` service. Now
  `plantumlAllowExternal` (or `DK_PLANTUML_ALLOW_EXTERNAL`) accepts exactly
  three values: unset (sandbox, the default, unchanged), a list of URL prefixes
  (allowlist mode), or `internet`. The build prints the declared entries, and
  `dockitty-assert-plantuml-no-remote-include` verifies that the running service
  matches them. An entry must end in `/` and may not carry `:80/` or `:443/`.
  Most sites need no change: bundled `<C4/...>` includes work in
  the default sandbox. See [ADR-0074](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0074-plantuml-external-include-opt-in.md)
  and [Allowing external includes](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/guides/consumer-setup.md#allowing-external-includes).

- **Any MCP client can read a DocKitty site's published artifacts (#284).**
  Before, an agent had to fetch and stitch `/api/index.json` and
  `/api/pages/*.json` itself. Now the new `@spec-kitty/doc-kitty-mcp`
  workspace package serves them over stdio: run `pnpm pack --filter
  @spec-kitty/doc-kitty-mcp`, install the tarball, and launch
  `doc-kitty-mcp --site <url>` or `--dir <dist>`. Registry publishing is
  deferred, so the tarball is the supported form. Every site's `/api/*.json`
  also gains `buildId` (to detect a torn read) and, on the index, `sections`.
  A site that sets `links: { mcp: true }` advertises the wiring in
  `_links.mcp` and `llms.txt`. See
  [ADR-0073](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0073-generic-mcp-server-over-published-artifacts.md) and
  the [MCP server quickstart](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/guides/mcp-server-quickstart.md).

- **The footer links the site's machine entry points on every page.** Before, an agent had to know the paths of `llms.txt`, the agent API and the rest. Now a `Machine-readable` group lists each one the site serves, with or without a theme, and never one it doesn't. Set `footer: { machineEntryPoints: false }` to remove the group, or `{ label: '...' }` to rename it. The `<head>` RSS and `llms.txt` links follow what the site serves too, so a site with no `rss.xml` route no longer advertises one. A site that sets `starlight.head` now gets these links too, where its entries used to replace the toolkit's `head`; if it added its own RSS alternate, the page now has two.

- **A group's title can be the link to its index page (#290).** Set `sidebar: { titleIsIndex: true }` and a generated sidebar group's label links to its index page, with no "Overview" entry below it, and a separate chevron opens and closes the group. A group with no index page keeps its plain toggle, and previous and next links are unchanged. The option is off by default, and with it off Starlight's own sidebar renders as before. It cannot be set together with `sidebar.indexLabel`. A sidebar you write yourself is not changed.

- **Every published, dated page gets an Atom entry at `/api/pages/<id>.atom.xml`.** Before, a page had only a JSON record. Now the toolkit injects the route on every site, with nothing to mount, and builds a deterministic Atom entry document with the page's rendered HTML. A draft or a page with no `updated` or `generated.at` date gets none. Set `pageFormats: { atom: false }` to turn it off. A static host picks the response `Content-Type` from the `.xml` extension, so `type=entry` is guaranteed only in the link that points at the entry. A site with no `site` gets no entries and no Atom links, with one build warning, because an Atom `id` must be a stable absolute IRI. An `.mdx` page's entry has no `<content>`, a local image becomes its alt text, and characters XML 1.0 forbids are removed from Atom and RSS output. The `id` changes when the domain, `base` or slug changes.

- **Each published page links its JSON, OKF and Atom versions, in the footer and the `<head>`.** A draft, a page outside the docs collection, or a page with `agent: { discoverable: false }` has none: that opt-out also hides the links (its `source` link stays, as that is for reading the file). Only the links go: the page's JSON, Atom and OKF files are still built and served. Set `repository: { provider, repo, branch, siteDir }` to add a `source` link to the page's file on GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket; a generated page has none, and self-hosted instances are not supported. The links are pills under the spec-kitty theme and plain links without it.

- **Pages and sections can show an icon in the sidebar (#293).** Set `sidebar.icon` on a page, or `icon` on a section in `sections.yaml` or a charter's `sections.entries`, to `fa-<name>` for Font Awesome's solid set or to the name of a Starlight built-in. A group takes its section's icon, or else its index page's. Only the icons you use reach the output, as inline SVG hidden from assistive technology, with no font file and no external request, and a page showing a Font Awesome icon carries one CC BY 4.0 licence comment. An unknown name fails the build and `validate-frontmatter`, naming the page or section. A site with no icons is unchanged. A sidebar you write yourself takes no icons, and the build warns once if any are authored.

### Changed

- **Metadata blocks start collapsed (#290).** Before, Who is this for, Related,
  External references and Glossary links used always showed in full, and on a
  page with several they pushed the content down. Now each starts closed behind a
  control with its label and count, such as "Related (3)". They open by mouse or
  keyboard, also with scripts off, start closed again on the next page, print
  open, and stay in search. Set `metadataBlocks: { collapsed: false }` to keep them
  open. See [ADR-0077](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0077-shared-disclosure-control.md).

- **Generated sidebar groups start closed (#290).** Before, the groups of the generated sidebar were open on every page, apart from any a site had set to collapse, such as the generated API groups. Now each starts closed, except the groups on the path to the current page, which Starlight opens by itself. Set `sidebar: { collapsed: false }` to keep the old sidebar exactly. A sidebar you write yourself is not changed.

### Fixed

- **The agent index no longer names a surface the site does not mount (#290).**
  Before, `/api/index.json` linked `rss`, `bibliography`, `scenarios`, `llms` and
  `sitemap`, and each record's `self`, unless the site turned the first four off
  through `links`, so a site without one of those routes shipped a dangling link.
  Now the toolkit detects the surfaces from the site's routes at their standard
  paths, and `_links` follows that. `llms` follows the `llms.txt` route, and
  `sitemap` needs both the sitemap and `site` to be set, so a build with no `site`
  has no `sitemap` link. `IndexLinks.llms` and `IndexLinks.sitemap` are now
  optional in the contract types. An explicit `links` value still wins for
  `rss`, `bibliography`, `scenarios` and `pages`, which is how to link a route at
  another path; `llms` and `sitemap` have no override.

## [0.6.0] — 2026-11-02

### Added

- **A site can publish versioned API reference pages from its OpenAPI files
  (#244).** Before, DocKitty had no API reference: authors linked to a separate
  Swagger site or pasted the spec into a page. Now an `openapi` option in
  `defineDocKittyIntegrations` takes OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 files, each with a
  `label` and `released` flag, and builds reference pages at
  `/reference/api/<label>/` inside the normal frame, with version links and an
  "unreleased" badge. Each version also publishes its raw file, byte for byte,
  and an `openapi.<ext>.sha256` that `sha256sum -c` checks, and gets a line in
  `llms.txt`. The option is off by default and needs two optional peers,
  `starlight-openapi@0.27.0` and `@astrojs/markdown-satteri@0.4.4`. A bad
  path, file or label fails the build with a `[dk-openapi]` error. A strict CSP
  needs one script hash and one style-attribute hash (with `'unsafe-hashes'`). See
  [Publish OpenAPI reference pages](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/guides/openapi-reference.md) and
  [ADR-0049](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0049-openapi-reference-via-existing-integration.md).

- **A `kind: Schematic` page documents a JSON or YAML schema (#245).** Before,
  a schema stayed a file that readers opened in a repository. Now a page with
  `kind: Schematic` and `schematic_path: <file>` (relative to the project root,
  inside it) keeps your own Markdown as the body. The toolkit adds the
  schema description before it, then `## Diagram`, `## Properties` and
  `## Source`; a `##` heading you write with one of those names replaces the
  generated one. `$ref` within the file or to another file in the root is
  followed, and a URL `$ref` renders as a link. A bad path, a parse error, a
  non-schema file or an unresolvable `$ref` fails the build with a
  `[dk-schematic]` error. The diagram needs build-mode diagrams and the
  PlantUML service, so client mode leaves it out. The schema is published
  unchanged beside the page, and the OKF export `resource` points at it. No new
  option; `yaml` is a new dependency. See
  [ADR-0067](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0067-schematic-pages-reference-a-schema.md).

- **A site can leave whole docs folders out of the build (#247).** Before, the
  docs loader refused any pattern but the default, so a folder you keep in git
  but do not publish (an archive, internal reports, working notes) was built,
  schema-checked and link-checked like any other. Now
  `defineDocKittyIntegrations({ exclude: ['archive', 'plans/engineering-notes'] })`
  leaves those folders out of the loader, the routes, the sidebar, search, the
  sitemap, `rss.xml`, `llms.txt`, the agent API and the ADR Hub, and
  `validate-frontmatter` and `check-links --strict` skip them. Entries are
  folder paths relative to `docsDir`, with no globs, and each must exist with the
  same letter case. A link or `related:` ref from a published page into an
  excluded folder is reported as "target is excluded from the site";
  `assert-no-broken-links` and `generate-adr-index` take a new `--docs <dir>`
  option to read the list. Without `exclude` nothing changes. See
  [ADR-0070](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0070-excluded-folders.md).

- **Date-named ADRs get real ids, order and status (#248).** Before, an ADR's
  id was always its leading four digits, so `2026-03-09-1-slug.md` read as
  `2026`. Its status came only from a body `## Status` section, and its date only
  from `updated`. Now a docs tree can set `adr.id` in `docs/_meta/charter.yaml`:
  `preset: date-seq` reads `2026-03-09-1` and orders by date, then by sequence
  number (`-2` before `-10`), and `pattern:` takes a regex with a named `id`
  group. When an ADR has no body `## Status`, its frontmatter `status` is shown,
  and when it has no `updated`, its frontmatter `date`. The generated ADR index
  and the hub's ADR cards still share one extractor. Without the axis nothing
  changes. `generate-adr-index.mjs` reads the charter next to `--dir`, or the
  one under the new `--docs-root`. See
  [ADR-0069](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0069-configurable-adr-id-and-frontmatter-status.md).

- **Old `.html` URLs keep working after a move from DocFX (#249).** Before,
  an Astro redirect keyed on `/a/b.html` was written as the folder
  `dist/a/b.html/index.html`, which a static host does not serve at
  `/a/b.html`. A key `/a/b/index.html` replaced the live page `/a/b/` with a
  folder, and the redirect-coverage gate could not check `.html` URLs at all.
  Now the `legacyHtmlRedirects` option of `defineDocKittyIntegrations`
  (`{ '/a/b.html': '/a/b/' }`, without the base) writes a flat
  `dist/a/b.html` stub after the build. The stub is `noindex`, has a canonical
  link to the target, and is not in the sitemap, `llms.txt` or the agent API.
  It works at the domain root and under a base path, and chains in the map are
  shortened to one step. The gate looks up a baselined `.html` URL as that
  file, follows chains, and fails on a missing stub or a dead target.
  `--declared-redirects` may now be repeated. The new
  `dockitty-generate-legacy-redirects` command writes the mechanical map
  (`x.html -> x/`, `x/index.html -> x/`) from a committed list of old URLs. See
  [ADR-0071](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0071-legacy-html-redirects-as-flat-stubs.md) and
  [Keeping .html URLs](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/migrations/legacy-html-urls.md).

- **GitHub alert blockquotes render as Starlight asides (#250).** Before, a
  `> [!NOTE]` blockquote rendered as a plain quote that started with a literal
  `[!NOTE]`, and converting it to `:::note` broke the page on GitHub. Now, with
  the new `githubAlerts: true` option, a top-level blockquote that opens with
  `[!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!WARNING]` or `[!CAUTION]` renders as
  the matching native aside: note, tip, note titled "Important", caution titled
  "Warning" and danger titled "Caution". They share the theme and accessible
  name of `:::note` and the Markua callouts. A plain quote, an unknown
  `[!X]` marker and a deck page are unchanged. Off by default, so existing
  sites render as before. See
  [ADR-0068](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0068-github-alerts-as-starlight-asides.md).

- **The link and frontmatter checks can leave a folder out.** Before, a folder
  of files that are not pages, such as changelog fragments in a repository's own
  `docs/`, could only be left out through a built site's `exclude` option. Now
  `dockitty-check-links` and `dockitty-validate-frontmatter` take
  `--exclude <folder>`, once per folder. The folder must exist inside one of the
  roots, or the command exits with status 2. See
  [ADR-0072](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0072-parallel-landing-without-shared-files.md).

### Changed

- **An Astro `redirects` key that ends in `.html` fails a static build
  (#249).** Before, it built a folder that a static host does not serve at that
  URL, or replaced a live page. Now a static build (`output: 'static'` with
  `build.redirects` on) stops and names each key. Move those entries to
  `legacyHtmlRedirects`, without the base on the target. A server-output
  (adapter) site, or one whose adapter sets `build.redirects: false`, keeps its
  `.html` keys: Astro writes no files for them, and the adapter (or Astro at
  request time) answers them. A key that is also a `legacyHtmlRedirects` source
  fails in every mode.

- **An `adr.id` pattern may be written in upper case (#271).** Before,
  `pattern: '^(?<id>ADR-\d+)-'` matched no ADR, because the pattern runs
  against the lowercased file name, and then (#269, never released) failed at
  charter load. Now such a pattern is matched case-insensitively, so it reads
  `ADR-12-Use-X.md` on the hub and in the generated index alike. The id shows
  lowercased (`adr-12`), so it agrees with the page's URL. Escapes such as `\D`
  and `\W`, group names and back-references keep their meaning. A lower-case
  pattern compiles exactly as before. See the amendment note in
  [ADR-0069](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0069-configurable-adr-id-and-frontmatter-status.md).

- **The ADR index is regenerated after merge, not in each PR.** Before, every
  PR that added an ADR also added a row to the table in `docs/adr/README.md`,
  and CI failed a stale table, so parallel PRs conflicted on it. Now a bot PR
  regenerates the table after merge, and CI checks per PR only that no two ADRs
  share a number, with the new `generate-adr-index.mjs --check-ids`. See
  [ADR-0072](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0072-parallel-landing-without-shared-files.md).

- **Changelog entries are fragment files.** Before, every PR added its entry
  to the one `[Unreleased]` section of `CHANGELOG.md`, so parallel PRs
  conflicted on the same lines. Now a PR adds one file under `docs/changelog/unreleased/`, and
  `pnpm changelog:release <version>` writes the fragments into the version
  section at release time. Released history is unchanged. The example site
  shows pending fragments as Unreleased. See
  [ADR-0072](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0072-parallel-landing-without-shared-files.md).

- A large JSON diagram stays at the size PlantUML drew it, and selecting it
  opens the same drawing centered at full size.

- **CI is ready for a merge queue, and a PR can pause its CI.** Before, CI ran
  only on pull requests and pushes, so a merge queue would have waited forever
  for `ci-ok`. Now `ci.yml` also runs on `merge_group`, and a PR labelled
  `pr:pause-ci` skips every lane with `ci-ok` red until the label goes. The CI
  helper tests run in CI, and a change to `.github/scripts`, `.github/actions`
  or `.github/filters.yml` runs every lane. See
  [ADR-0072](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0072-parallel-landing-without-shared-files.md).

### Security

- **The PlantUML render service is pinned by digest and refuses remote
  includes (#251).** Before, every workflow ran the floating
  `plantuml/plantuml-server:jetty` tag, so a re-tag silently changed the renderer.
  The server also ran with its default `INTERNET` profile, so a diagram with
  `!includeurl` (or an `!include` of a URL) was fetched at build time. Now
  `ci.yml`, `deploy.yml` and `update-a11y-baselines.yml` run
  `jetty-v1.2026.9@sha256:065c66ad…` with `PLANTUML_SECURITY_PROFILE=SANDBOX`.
  Such a diagram renders as an error and fails the build. A new bin,
  `dockitty-assert-plantuml-no-remote-include`, proves this against a live
  service, and CI runs it before building: it serves a canary, checks that the
  canary is reachable from inside the service container, and requires the
  `!includeurl` and `!include <url>` fixtures to be refused with zero canary
  requests. The consumer guide now shows the hardened service block. To adopt
  it, copy that block; a diagram that includes a URL or a local file will then
  stop the build.

### Documentation

- **The setup guide says how to write redirect targets for a site at the domain
  root (#261).** Before, a config that built its Astro `redirects` targets as
  `` `${BASE}${to}` `` with `BASE = '/'` produced `//new/`, which a browser reads as
  a link to another host. The guide now says to use `''` at the root or strip the
  trailing slash, and the example config strips it.

## [0.5.0] — 2026-10-25

### 💥 Breaking

- **`validate-frontmatter` requires `kind` on every page again (#219).**
  Before, the gate accepted a page without `kind` (since #38), while the
  convention, ADR-0009 and the charter said it was required. Now a page without
  `kind` fails with `` `kind`: required ``, the bundle-root `README.md`
  included. The build still renders such a page, and an unknown `kind` value
  still only warns. To keep the old behaviour, list `kind` under
  `required_fields.optional` in `docs/_meta/charter.yaml`. See
  [ADR-0065](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0065-kind-required-again.md) and
  [Upgrading from 0.4.0 to 0.5.0](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/migrations/0.4-to-0.5.md).

### Changed

- **On screens wider than the frame, the sidebar tint now reaches the screen edge
  (#224).** Before, above the 120rem default cap the sidebar panel's tint started
  at the frame edge, so it looked like a block floating 320px in under a header
  that runs edge to edge. Now the panel's tint runs out to the viewport's start
  edge, as the header bar does, and its links stay on the frame. Nothing changes
  at or below 1920px, or on a full-width frame. Recorded in
  [ADR-0066](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0066-sidebar-tint-bleeds-past-the-frame.md).

### Fixed

- **The table of contents rail no longer jumps across the page on a slow first
  paint (#223).** Before, if the browser painted before the reading pane was
  parsed, the rail (or, collapsed, its 1px line) was drawn next to the left
  sidebar and then jumped to its place, a layout shift of about 0.25. Now it is
  in its final place in every paint. Nothing moves once the page has loaded.
- **The collapsed reading column clears the rail toggle under any frame cap
  (#220).** Before, a site that capped the frame between 72rem and 84rem and was
  viewed on a wider screen had the collapsed column run 7px under the toggle.
  The column's end padding is now worked out from the width of the row the pane
  and rail share, not from the viewport. The default frame is unchanged.
- **The load-shift layout test no longer flakes (#222).** It counted shifts
  from Starlight's own markup still parsing in, and failed in about a quarter of
  runs under parallel load. It now paints the whole page first, then runs the
  enhancement and counts every shift, still requiring exactly 0, with a
  positive control that proves a real shift is caught. It runs against the
  published build again.
- **Agent page records now give an absolute `source` (#236).** Before, on a
  site with a base, `source` was a site-relative path that returned a 404.
  Now it is absolute, includes the base, and equals `_links.self.href` and the
  `source` in the agent index.
- **OKF export links work on sites with a base (#237).** Before, links between
  pages and links to site files lost the base or pointed one folder too deep.
  Now `.md` links resolve against the linking page and become bundle paths, and
  other site links carry `<site><base>`. `--site-url` takes the origin and the
  export adds the base. The advisory link check also reports unresolved relative
  links.
- **OKF export keeps the prose of section `README` files (#238).** Before, the
  export dropped the body of a section `README`, so its text and links were
  missing from the bundle. Now a `README` with body text is written as a page at
  `<id>.md`, such as `guides/README.md`, with its links rewritten. The section
  `index.md` stays a strict OKF entry list and lists that page first. A
  `README` with no body exports as before.
- **Written-out and numeric dates read the same on every build machine
  (#234).** Before, a non-ISO value with no zone, such as `updated: May 1,
  2024` or `1/2/24`, was read in the build machine's time zone, so the same
  source gave different instants, feed order and agent-API dates. In
  Pacific/Auckland, `May 1, 2024` became `2024-04-30T12:00:00Z`. Now it is read
  as UTC, like an ISO value with no zone, and so is a rolled-over one such as
  `2024-04-31T10:00`. A value that names its zone (`GMT`, `UTC`, `Z`, `EST`, or
  `+0200` after the time) keeps it. The gate still recommends
  `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.
- **The example's Cucumber report regenerates byte-identically (#231).**
  Before, every regeneration of `example/reports/cucumber.ndjson` was a diff of
  hundreds of lines, from machine details, timestamps and random ids. Now
  `src/scripts/normalise-cucumber-report.mjs` fixes them: meta, timestamps (to
  a named `--at` instant), durations, ids, and the run directory in stack
  traces. `PROVENANCE.txt` ends the procedure with it, and a test fails if the
  committed report is not normalised.
- **Decision-index lock files are no longer tracked (#232).** Seven older
  missions still tracked a transient `kitty-specs/**/decisions/index.json.lock`.
  They are removed from the index; the `.gitignore` rule keeps them out.

## [0.4.0] — 2026-10-19

This release moves the toolkit to Astro 7.4 and Starlight 0.42.6, and needs
Node 22.22.0 or later. Pages render as they did on 0.3.0: heading anchor links
stay off and the HTML keeps its whitespace. Readers get a full-window view for
diagrams and images, a draft notice on draft pages, and a sidebar that no longer
jumps. Authors get Gherkin authoring aids and a `Specification` layout for
feature pages. Every build publishes a content graph and an OKF export bundle,
and the agent API is now version 3. The page frame is capped at 120rem by
default. The release removes what 0.3.0 deprecated, so committed generated pages
must be regenerated once, and it rejects a date field that is not a date.
**Upgrading from 0.3.0: read the Breaking section and the
[0.3 to 0.4 migration guide](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/migrations/0.3-to-0.4.md) first.**

### 💥 Breaking

- **Install Astro 7, Starlight 0.42 and `@astrojs/markdown-remark` 7, on Node
  22.22.0 or later (#119, #144, #145, #146).** Before, the toolkit needed
  Astro 5 and Starlight 0.32. Now its peer ranges are `astro >=7.2.10 <8`,
  `@astrojs/starlight >=0.42.0 <0.43.0` and `@astrojs/markdown-remark >=7.3.0
  <8`, and `engines.node` is `>=22.22.0`. Run
  `pnpm add astro@^7.4.0 @astrojs/starlight@^0.42.6 @astrojs/markdown-remark@^7.3.3`
  and use Node 22.22 or later locally and in CI. The toolkit sets Astro's
  Markdown processor to `unified()` itself (ADR-0060), so remark and rehype
  plugins you add through `markdown.remarkPlugins` / `rehypePlugins` keep
  working; do not set `markdown.processor` yourself. Astro 7 and Starlight 0.42
  bring their own breaking changes for code you wrote outside the toolkit, such
  as your own components or pages; see their upgrade guides.
- **Build schema extensions on zod 4 via `astro/zod`: the exported docs schema
  (`./schema`) is now a zod 4 schema.** Before, it was built on zod 3. Now it
  imports from `astro/zod`, and `.default(...)` becomes `.prefault(...)`
  semantics (the default is parsed through the schema, not returned as is). If
  you extend `docKittyDocsSchema` with your own fields, import `z` from
  `astro/zod` and write them for zod 4; a zod 3 schema no longer composes with
  it.
- **Read the producer from `generated_by`: `api/scenarios.json` no longer has
  `generated_from`, and its `version` is `"2"` (#183).** Before, every record
  carried `generated_from: "doc-kitty/gherkin"` next to `generated_by`, with
  `version: "1"`. Now `generated_from` is gone and `version` is `"2"`; nothing
  else in the record moved. Clients that read `generated_from` or pin version
  `"1"` need updating.
- **Regenerate committed Gherkin and glossary pages once: the 0.3.0 stamps now
  fail the frontmatter check (#210).** Before, a page stamped with the
  unversioned `generated.by: doc-kitty/gherkin` or `doc-kitty/glossary`, or
  with a `sha256:` hash in `generated.at`, was still treated as generated. Now
  such a stamp is retired: the page is no longer exempt as a generated page,
  and `dockitty-validate-frontmatter` fails it with a message that names the
  regeneration step. Run `dockitty-generate-feature-pages` for Gherkin pages,
  and `astro build` (or `astro dev`) for glossary pages; both still own and
  overwrite pages with a retired stamp, and write the versioned
  `<producer>/<version>` stamp with `content_hash`. Commit the result.
- **Read `updated` as a full UTC timestamp in the agent API, now version 3
  (#177).** Before, `api/index.json` reported `version: "2"` and each page's
  `updated` as a date such as `2026-10-18`. Now it reports `version: "3"` and
  `updated` as `2026-10-18T00:00:00Z`. Agents or scripts that pin the version
  or parse a date-only value need updating. Nothing else in the record moved.
- **Produce the Gherkin report before every CI docs build, or set
  `gherkin.results.required: false` (#166).** Before, a missing
  `gherkin.results` report only logged a warning and the site built without
  results, so a CI job could publish a site with no results unnoticed. Now, when
  the `CI` environment variable holds anything other than empty, `false` or `0`,
  a missing report stops the build and the message names the report and the
  opt-out. GitHub Actions sets `CI=true` in every job, so preview and docs-only
  jobs without a report are the ones that fail. Run Cucumber in the same job
  first, or download its report as an artifact. For jobs that never run the
  tests, set
  `gherkin: { results: { report: 'reports/cucumber.ndjson', required: false } }`
  and they warn as before. Local builds still warn only. An unreadable or
  malformed report fails as it did.
- **The page frame is capped at 120rem by default (#205).** Before, the frame
  spanned the viewport unless a site set `--dk-width-frame`. Now the default is
  `120rem`. Viewports of 1920px and narrower look as before. On a wider
  viewport the frame is 1920px wide and centred: at 2560px a rail page has
  192px beside the column instead of 512px. To keep a full-width frame, set
  `:root { --dk-width-frame: 100%; }`. A site that already sets the token is
  unaffected. See
  [Cap the page width](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/guides/consumer-setup.md#cap-the-page-width) and
  [ADR-0064](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0064-default-frame-cap.md).
- **Write every date as a date, not a bare number or a short string: the build
  and the frontmatter gate now reject what they accepted before (#227).**
  Before, the build took anything JavaScript's `Date` could parse for `updated`,
  `stale_after`, `generated.at` and `verified[].at`, and the gate passed `1`,
  `"1"`, `"2024"` and `20241001` with a warning, so `updated: 1` built and
  published a wrong date. Now a value must have a date shape and `Date` must read
  it: a YAML date, ISO-8601, `YYYY-MM`, a string with a month name and a number,
  or one with three or more numeric groups (the last three draw a `nonIso`
  advisory). Numbers, `"1/2"`, `"abc 2024"`, `"2024.5"` and `18/10/2026` fail,
  in both, with a message that names the field and `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`. A
  retired `sha256:` stamp in `generated.at` is also rejected by the build, where
  only the gate did before. To list every page in one pass, run
  `dockitty-validate-frontmatter docs`, then fix each, for example
  `updated: 2024-10-01T00:00:00Z`. See the
  [ADR-0059 note](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0059-content-graph-and-okf-alignment.md#per-output-dates-and-the-date-shape-rule-226-227).

### Added

- **Readers can expand diagrams and images to the full window again (#185).**
  Before, sites built on the toolkit drew diagrams and images at page width
  with no way to enlarge them; the older portal sites had a lightbox that the
  toolkit never carried over. Now every diagram has an expand button, and every
  image in page content expands on click or Enter. It opens in a modal that
  closes with Esc, the close button or a click outside, and focus returns to
  where it was. It is on for every site, with no option and no new dependency.
  Its labels are English only for now (#161).
- **Every build publishes `api/content-graph.json` (#176).** Before, an agent
  or tool that wanted the site's structure fetched one JSON file per page, and
  nothing held the reverse edges. Now one file lists every published page,
  persona, catalog entry and external resource, plus each frontmatter relation
  between them (`related`, `audience`, `cites`, `in-section`, `derived-from`).
  It is built by the same resolvers as the rendered blocks, sorted for
  identical bytes on every build, linked from `api/index.json`, and drafts stay
  out. The artifact gate fails on any edge that points nowhere.
- **Export a plain OKF v0.2 bundle (#178).** Before, OKF readers saw a DocKitty
  site as unconnected pages, because they only follow body links. Now every
  build writes `dist/okf/`, and `dockitty-export-okf` writes the same bundle on
  demand. Relations become `/`-prefixed body links, links to pages point at
  bundle paths, index files take OKF form, and `doc_status`, `updated` and
  authors map to OKF `status`, `generated` and actors. A built-in checker
  (`--check`) verifies OKF §11. Drafts are left out.
- **Translate the sidebar "Overview" label, or set it once (#161).** Before, the
  index entry of a nested group read "Overview" in English on every site. Now the
  word is the UI string `dockitty.sidebar.indexLabel`: translate it in your
  Starlight `i18n` files and each language shows its own word. To set one label
  for all languages, use `defineDocKittyIntegrations({ sidebar: { indexLabel:
  'Intro' } })`; it wins over the translation. The `sidebar` option accepts
  either the Starlight sidebar array you may already pass or this
  `{ indexLabel }` object; an unknown key or a blank label stops the build.
  Previous and next links keep the page title. With neither set, your sidebar is
  unchanged.
- **A stale report now says so on a single scenario (#166).** Before, a
  `::gherkin{src=… scenario=…}` include showed nothing when the report was made
  from another version of the file, so the missing result looked like a gap.
  Now its result line reads "Results not shown: the test report was made from a
  different version of this file."
- **A hand-mounted scenarios route without results warns (#166).** Before, a
  site with its own `src/pages/api/scenarios.json` route that called
  `scenarioIndexRoute()` without `results` served an index with no results and
  no sign why. Now, while `gherkin.results` is set, the build logs one warning
  per `astro build` and one per `astro dev` run, naming the route file and the
  value to pass.
- **Follow `_links` through the agent API instead of building URLs (#103).**
  Before, `api/index.json` and the per-page records held no links, so an agent
  had to know the URL scheme. Now the index links to itself, `llms.txt` and the
  sitemap, plus the feed, bibliography and scenarios routes you mount. Each
  record links to its per-page JSON, its HTML page and its related pages, and a
  per-page record also links up to the index. The keys are additive; the index
  `version` is `'3'` because of the `updated` change (#177). The `links` option on `agentIndexRoute` and
  `agentPageRoute` defaults to all on, as in the worked example; pass `false`
  for a surface your site does not mount. If you mount the index elsewhere,
  pass `indexPath` to both routes, and keep it ending in `/api/index.json`.
  `pnpm assert:artifacts` now fails when a `_links` href in `dist/api/` points
  at a file the build did not produce. See
  [ADR-0058](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0058-build-state-owner-and-config-split.md).
- **Point the build check at a moved agent index with `--index-path` (#172).**
  Before, `assert:artifacts` read only `dist/api/index.json`, so a site that
  mounts the index elsewhere (`indexPath: '/v2/api/index.json'`) could not run
  the check. Now `assert:artifacts --index-path v2/api/index.json` moves every
  index check to that file. The path is relative to `dist` (without the site
  base). The check takes the base from the index's `self` link and follows
  `_links` to other JSON files wherever they sit. One leading `/` is ignored; a
  value containing `..`, an empty value, or a drive or `//` path exits 2.
  Without the flag, nothing changes.
- **Set a glossary context once per folder with
  `gherkin.defaultGlossaryContext` (#197).** Before, a generated feature page
  got `glossary_context` only from a `@dk:context` tag on each feature. Now a
  map such as `{ shipping: 'shipping', 'shipping/eu': 'customs' }` gives every
  page under a source folder its context. The longest matching folder wins,
  compared by whole folder name, and a feature's own `@dk:context` tag still
  wins over it. The drift gate takes the same map as repeated
  `--default-glossary-context <dir>=<context>` flags. A key that matches no
  feature folder warns, and the site build warns about a context the glossary
  does not define (ADR-0061).
- **Turn on the imperative-step lint with `gherkin.lint.imperativeSteps`
  (#196).** Before, nothing checked for steps
  such as `When I click "#book-button"`. Now, when the option is on, the build
  warns about each Given or When step that names a UI action (click, tap, fill
  in, …) or quotes a CSS selector, on generated feature pages and in-page
  `gherkin` fences. It is off by default, never fails a build and never changes
  a page. `verbs`, `extend` and `keywords` adjust the phrase list and scope.
  Includes, `gherkin raw` fences and non-English features are not checked
  (ADR-0061).
- **Silence the imperative-step lint with `@dk:allow=imperative` (#196).** The
  tag works on a
  Feature, a Rule or a Scenario, and is the first `@dk:` tag read below
  Feature level. Any other value warns (ADR-0061).
- **Feature pages show their tags and source in a header card (#198).** The
  new base-kind `Specification` layout renders a labelled card above the
  scenarios.
  The source is a link when the site sets `sourceUrlPrefix`. The "On this page"
  list stays the scenario list, and the results summary stays in the body. A
  theme opts out by mapping `layouts.Specification` to `Default.astro`
  (ADR-0062).
- **Every draft page shows a draft notice (#198).** Before, a draft page looked
  exactly like an active one. Now a draft page of any kind shows "Draft. This
  page is a work in progress and may change." under its title when drafts are
  built. The site root is never shown as a draft, and out-of-frame slide decks
  are not covered (ADR-0062).
- **The current sidebar entry is revealed before first paint (#203).** Before,
  the reveal ran from a head script after the page had loaded. Now `Sidebar` is
  the toolkit's sixth carrier: it renders Starlight's own sidebar unchanged and
  then the script that reveals the current entry. Like the other carriers, it
  replaces a `Sidebar` override passed through `starlight.components`. A
  Starlight plugin that overrides `Sidebar` still wins over the carrier, and the
  reveal is then lost: such a plugin must render the toolkit's `Sidebar`. See
  [ADR-0063](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0063-sidebar-carrier.md).
- **The accessibility lane also checks the published sidebar (#200).** Before,
  it measured only the drafts-on build, so the sidebar readers see was never
  checked. Now CI also serves `example/dist-nodrafts` to two more Playwright
  projects, `published-light` and `published-dark`, which run the sidebar
  specs. A new spec checks that draft entries appear only in the drafts-on
  sidebar and that previous and next links skip drafts in the published build.
  The server stops when the dist and the draft mode it was given disagree.
- **Every machine surface is compared across builds (#201).** The sitemap,
  RSS feed, `llms.txt` files, `api/` JSON, the OKF bundle and the Pagefind
  index must be byte-identical between two builds with the same draft setting.
  Between the drafts-on and drafts-off builds only the drafts' own page records
  may differ. Each surface must match at least one file, so a renamed surface
  fails the check instead of dropping out.
- **The page chrome has an explicit target-size check (#202).** Every link and
  button in the header, sidebar, rail and footer must be at least 24 by 24 CSS
  px, or meet the WCAG 2.2 spacing exception. It runs at 1280px and 1920px with
  the rail expanded and collapsed, and on a phone with the menu open.
- **The column on a page with a rail and no sidebar is checked to be centred
  (#199).** Before, this was a code-review item. Now a Playwright spec measures
  it at each width, with the rail expanded and collapsed.
- **The stock-header fixture has a stamp, and `pnpm fixture:stock-header`
  recaptures it (#207).** The fixture that the `Header` carrier is compared
  with is now captured from a build with the carrier switched off, so it is
  Starlight's own header. `stock-header.meta.json` records the Starlight and
  Astro versions and the `compressHTML` setting it was captured with, and a fast
  test names the field that no longer matches and the command to run.

### Changed

- **The toolkit sets Starlight `markdown.processedDirs` itself.** Before, only
  `src/content/docs` got Starlight's Markdown processing. Now the docs root is
  listed first, any directory you list under `starlight.markdown.processedDirs`
  follows, de-duplicated, and your other `markdown` options are merged in.
- **The scenarios API names its producer in `generated_by` (#182).** Before,
  `api/scenarios.json` named its producer only as
  `generated_from: "doc-kitty/gherkin"`, while the generated feature pages'
  stamp says `doc-kitty-gherkin/<version>`. Now it carries
  `generated_by: "doc-kitty-gherkin/<version>"`, an OKF tool actor matching
  that stamp. `generated_from` is removed in this same release (#183, see
  Breaking).
- **Metadata follows OKF v0.2 (#177).** Before, `updated` was a date,
  `okf_version` sat only on the root index, and authors were email addresses.
  Now `updated` and `stale_after` take UTC timestamps
  (`2026-10-18T09:30:00Z`), every index declares `okf_version: "0.2"`, and
  `authors`, `generated.by` and `verified[].by` use OKF actors (`human:<id>`,
  `<tool>/<version>`, `process:<id>`). Old forms still build, with a warning
  from the doc checks. Generated Gherkin and glossary pages name the tool and
  version that wrote them, and keep `generated.at` unchanged until their
  content changes. Date-times without a zone are now read as UTC; before they
  were read in the build machine's local time, so such values may shift by its
  offset. Newly scaffolded pages carry a `generated:` stamp that records
  provenance only and grants no generated-page exemption. The metadata model
  documents how `doc_status` maps to OKF `status`.
- **The env reader honours `vite.envDir` and `--mode`, so drafts follow the
  files your build uses (#115).** This affects sites that set `vite.envDir` or
  build with a custom mode. Before, DocKitty read `.env*` files only from the
  site directory and always used `production` (or `development` for `astro
  dev`), so `DK_PUBLISH_DRAFTS` in `envDir`, or in `.env.staging`, was ignored.
  Now a relative `envDir` is read from the site directory, `envDir: false` reads
  no files, and `--mode staging` reads `.env.staging`. The mode `local` is
  refused, as in Vite. The process environment still wins. The gates follow
  your config's `envDir`; `dockitty-assert-build-artifacts` and
  `dockitty-check-redirect-coverage` without `--docs` stop when the config
  mentions `envDir` unless you pass `--env-dir <dir|false>`. Sites with neither
  setting are unchanged.
- **Heading anchor links stay off, as on 0.3.0 (#144).** Starlight 0.34 and
  later add a link icon to every heading by default. The toolkit sets
  Starlight's `markdown.headingLinks: false`, so headings, decks and the
  accessibility baselines look as they did. To turn the anchors on, pass
  `starlight: { markdown: { headingLinks: true } }` to
  `defineDocKittyIntegrations`.
- **The toolkit sets `compressHTML: true`, overriding your own setting
  (#145).** Astro 7 defaults to `compressHTML: 'jsx'`, which drops the
  whitespace between inline elements, so copied text and search excerpts read
  "status:activeUpdated". The toolkit's integration pins `compressHTML: true`,
  the pre-Astro-7 output, and it runs after your `astro.config.mjs`, so a
  `compressHTML` you set there has no effect. A configurable option may follow.
- **A build with broken docs pages stops at the first one (#119).** Before, the
  build listed every docs page with invalid frontmatter in one run. Astro 7's
  content sync stops at the first invalid entry, so you now see one page per
  run. Run `dockitty-validate-frontmatter docs` first to see them all at once.
  Render errors, such as a broken Gherkin fence, also stop the build at the
  first page, and the frontmatter check does not find them; the old
  "N Gherkin error(s) on M pages" summary is no longer printed.
- `RouteShapingOptions` no longer has `unpublishedDirs` or `unpublishedPaths`;
  the withheld drafts now travel in a per-config build state. The type is an
  internal seam, not supported API.
- **Draft pages gain one `p.dk-draft-notice` in their HTML (#198).** Pages that
  are not drafts are unchanged.
- **Existing `@dk:context` tags are now checked against the glossary (#197).**
  Before, a tag naming a context the glossary does not define was silently
  ignored for disambiguation. Now the site build warns about it, even on a site
  that does not set `defaultGlossaryContext`. The warning never fails the build
  or changes a page.
- **Feature pages use the `Specification` layout by default.** Before,
  `kind: Specification` fell back to the `Default` layout. Now it uses the new
  layout, so pages with tags or a source gain the card.
- **The example site maps its shipping and HR folders to glossary contexts.**
  The three shipping features no longer carry `@dk:context=shipping`, and the
  HR page now resolves `policy` to the HR definition. The example also turns on
  the imperative-step lint, with zero warnings.
- **The column shift between pages with and without a rail is intended
  (#204).** A page without a rail starts its column further along, by 144px
  from a 1600px viewport. Stock Starlight shifts too, and reserving a rail on
  every page was rejected. See
  [Collapsible TOC rail](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/architecture/collapsible-toc-rail.md#rail-and-no-rail-pages-the-column-shift-is-accepted).
- **The sidebar reveal script moved from `head` to the `Sidebar` carrier.** It
  is now one inline script right after the sidebar markup, and the `head`
  entry is gone.

### Fixed

- **Every RSS item has a `<pubDate>` (#190).** Before, generated Gherkin
  feature pages and glossary pages, which carry no `updated`, were feed items
  with no date, so feed readers sorted them unpredictably. Now an item takes its
  date from `updated`, else from the page's `generated.at` stamp, and the feed
  is ordered by that date. A page with neither is left out of the feed, with a
  build warning. A generated page without `updated` is dated by its
  `generated.at`, so it moves in the feed when the generator regenerates it.
- **Every page has exactly one `<h1>` (#191).** Before, a page whose body
  started with `# Title` rendered two: Starlight's title and the body heading.
  Now the first body H1 that repeats the frontmatter `title` is removed,
  wherever it sits, and links to its anchor still work. Any other body H1
  becomes an H2, so the title stays the page's only `<h1>`. Slide decks are
  unchanged. You do not need to edit your Markdown.
- **Shared links show a full card on Slack, WhatsApp and LinkedIn (#180).**
  Before, the spec-kitty theme's share image was an SVG, which those platforms
  do not show, and the card carried no image size or type. Now every page's
  `og:image` is a 1200x630 PNG with `og:image:width`, `og:image:height` and
  `og:image:type`, and the site-wide card's alt text is the site title. A page
  whose `social_thumb` or `hero_image` is an SVG gets the site-wide card, with a
  build warning. A theme whose `assets.socialImage` is an SVG gets the toolkit's
  default card, with a warning to give it a PNG or JPEG.
- **Generated hub pages no longer appear as RSS items (#127).** Before, the
  section and folder indexes the Gherkin generator writes, and the generated
  glossary index, showed up in `rss.xml` with no news of their own. Now
  generated hubs stay out of the feed; authored hubs are unchanged.
- **The home page's address no longer redirects (#188).** Before, the home
  page's canonical URL, its `og:url` and its sitemap entry had no trailing
  slash (`…/doc-kitty`), and GitHub Pages answered that address with a 301.
  Now all three end in `/`. This reverses the 0.2.x choice of a slash-less
  root sitemap entry; every other page is unchanged.
- **Footer "Back to top" jumps to the top again (#187).** Before, it linked
  `#top`, an anchor no page has. Now it links `#_top`.
- **`llms.txt` no longer has an empty heading (#189).** Before, the root group
  was headed `## ` when the section registry had no root label. Now it is
  `## Overview`.
- **`astro dev` shows the theme and the favicon on every request (#170).**
  Before, a theme stylesheet request with a query such as `?inline` rendered
  the page unthemed, and a site with a `base` got a 404 for its favicon at the
  path without the base. Built sites were never affected.
- **Glossary links on Markua pages match the build (#113).** Before, the page's
  "terms used" block re-read a Markua page without the Markua passes, so its
  links could differ from the page's. Now it replays them when `markua: true`.
- **A second DocKitty config in the same process (for example a test suite) no
  longer inherits the first config's draft-publication setting (#167).** Before,
  `defineDocKittyIntegrations` left the first config's internal environment
  values in place, so the second config read the first one's setting. Now each
  config starts with those values cleared. Production builds, which define one
  config per process, were not affected.
- **The build gates now follow the `envDir` of an imported base config, and a
  broken config stops them (#173).** Before, `assert-build-artifacts` and
  `check-redirect-coverage` searched the config's text for `envDir`, so a value
  set in an imported base config went unseen and a comment could trigger a
  failure. Now `assert-build-artifacts`, `check-redirect-coverage` and
  `check-links` evaluate `astro.config.*` and honour the base config's
  `envDir`. They exit 2 when the config will not evaluate, times out, or is not
  the config that decides the site root. `--astro-config` picks the config;
  `--env-dir <dir|false>` skips evaluation. An `envDir` set in an integration's
  `updateConfig` hook, and configs that vary by build mode, are still not seen.
- **A retired generator stamp names the right regeneration step (#210).** The
  frontmatter error for a retired glossary stamp pointed at the Gherkin
  generator. Now it names `dockitty-generate-feature-pages` for Gherkin pages
  and a site build for glossary pages.
- **The Markua showcase no longer requests a missing image (#194).** Before,
  its web-image figure loaded `https://example.com/mac.jpg`, which does not
  exist. Now it loads the site's own `macintosh.svg` by its absolute site URL,
  so it still shows web-URL passthrough. `dockitty-assert-no-broken-links`
  takes an opt-in `--no-external-images` (with `--allow-image-host <host>`)
  that fails a built `<img>` loaded from another host, or a same-site absolute
  image missing from the build, without fetching anything; the example's
  `pnpm assert:no-broken-links` turns it on.
- **The sidebar no longer jumps on a first visit (#203).** Before, the sidebar
  painted at the top and scrolled to the current entry only after the whole
  page had loaded, which took seconds on a slow link. Now the entry is in view
  at first paint, once the sidebar markup has arrived. In-session navigation
  still restores the position Starlight saved.
- **The header search starts where the column starts (#216).** Before, it sat
  24px before the column on a rail page and 168px off with the rail collapsed.
  Now it lines up with the column on pages with and without a rail, with the
  frame capped or not. A site title wider than the space before the column
  keeps the search after the title, as stock Starlight does.
- **The column no longer runs under the collapsed rail toggle (#217).** From
  1152 to 1296px with the rail collapsed, the column ran 7px under the toggle.
  Now, below 84rem (1344px), the pane's end padding with the rail collapsed is
  the toggle's width plus 4px.
- **The Persona card no longer leaves a large blank at wide widths (#206).**
  `--dk-width-passport` now defaults to the metadata band's width, 50rem
  instead of 32rem, and the card is start-aligned with the text below it. The
  card now follows `--dk-width-band`, so a site that sets `--dk-width-band` also
  resizes the card. A site can still set `--dk-width-passport` itself.
- **The OKF export no longer credits a human edit to the scaffold (#226).**
  Before, the export took `generated.by`, `at` and `content_hash` from any
  `generated` stamp, so a page that began as a scaffold and was then rewritten
  was exported as generated by `doc-kitty-scaffold`. Now only an ownership
  stamp (`doc-kitty-gherkin/<version>` or `doc-kitty-glossary/<version>`)
  supplies them. For any other stamp, `by` is the first author, who leaves
  `authors`, else `process:dockitty-export`, and `at` is `updated`, else that
  stamp's `at`. RSS still dates an item from `updated`, else `generated.at`,
  and the agent API is unchanged. See the
  [ADR-0059 note](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0059-content-graph-and-okf-alignment.md#per-output-dates-and-the-date-shape-rule-226-227).

### Documentation

- **The site's changelog shows every release, from CHANGELOG.md (#192).**
  Before, the example site's changelog was a hand-written page that stopped at
  v0.1.0. Now `/changelog/releases/` renders the repository's `CHANGELOG.md` at
  build time, so there is no copy to keep in sync, and `pnpm assert:changelog`
  fails when a `## [x.y.z]` release is missing from the built page.
- **Install 0.4.0 from the site's new install guide (#193).** Before, the site
  had no install guide and Getting started showed repository-internal commands.
  Now `/guides/install/` covers Node `>=22.22.0`, the astro 7, Starlight 0.42
  and `@astrojs/markdown-remark` 7 peers, the GitHub Packages `.npmrc` setup
  and the first build, and links the 0.3 to 0.4 migration guide; Getting
  started points consumers there. A test keeps the guide's Node floor, peer
  ranges, package name and wiring equal to `src/package.json` and the
  consumption-test fixture.
- **ADR-0061 and ADR-0062 record the decisions.** The consumer setup guide, the
  authoring guide, the Gherkin architecture page and the theming page cover the
  new options, the tag, the layout and the notice.

### Known limitations

- Every build logs `The collection "i18n" does not exist or is empty` and one
  `Could not render /presentations/<deck> from route /[...slug]` warning per
  deck page (#144, spike B17). Both are harmless: Starlight 0.42 looks up an
  optional `i18n` collection that a site without translation files does not
  have, and Starlight's catch-all route yields to the higher-priority
  `/presentations/[...slug]` deck route, which is the intended page. Defining
  an empty `i18n` collection only replaces the warning with another, and
  keeping deck pages out of Starlight's route needs a change to how decks are
  collected, so both are left for a later release.
- With a frame cap between 72rem and 84rem on a wider viewport, the column can
  still run under the collapsed rail toggle (#220). The 120rem default is not
  affected.
- Above the 120rem cap, the sidebar's tint starts at the frame edge while the
  header bar spans the viewport (#224, open design decision).
- On a slow first paint, Starlight's rail can be drawn next to the left sidebar
  and then jump into place (#223). The layout-shift check counts such
  partial-paint shifts and can flake under parallel load (#222); it runs in the
  `light` project only until it is redesigned.

## [0.3.0] — 2026-10-14

This release lets you write Gherkin scenarios in any page, shows their test
results from your Cucumber report, rewrites relative
Markdown links to working routes, widens the reading column to 60rem and makes
sidebars stop repeating their own labels. You now set index names in one place,
on `defineDocKittyIntegrations`, and the DocKitty commands read them from your
site config. Several silent problems now stop the build with a message that
names the file: two files at one address, a misspelt theme slot, empty Gherkin
sources. **Upgrading from 0.2.0: read the Breaking section first.**

### 💥 Breaking

- **Remove `--index-basename` from your CI scripts: the DocKitty commands now
  read index names from `astro.config.*` (#136).** Before, each command took its
  own index names, and `dockitty-check-links` accepted both `README` and `index`
  while the build used only `README`. Now `dockitty-check-links`,
  `dockitty-validate-frontmatter`, `dockitty-check-redirect-coverage`,
  `dockitty-generate-feature-pages`, `dockitty-new-doc` and `dockitty-scaffold`
  read your site config (about one extra second per run) and print the names they
  used. With no config next to the docs folder, they warn and use `README`; pass
  `--astro-config <path>` if your config lives elsewhere. A missing or broken
  config path exits 2. If you keep the flag, it must list the same names as the
  config (order and letter case aside), or the command exits 2.
- **Move `indexBasename` from `docKittyDocsLoader` to `defineDocKittyIntegrations`
  in `astro.config.*` (#136).** Before, you could set index names on the
  integration, the loader and the command line, and they could disagree. Now the
  integration is the only place, and the loader takes the value from it. If the
  loader still sets a different value, the build stops and shows both. Once the
  names are on the integration, delete the loader option. See
  [ADR-0050](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0050-route-collisions-and-single-index-setting.md).
- **Keep one file per page address: two files served at the same address now stop
  the build (#135).** Before, a folder with both `README.md` and `index.md` built
  with a warning, and `page.md` next to `page.mdx`, or two names that differ only
  in letter case, went unnoticed. Now the build, `dockitty-check-links --strict`
  (exit 1) and `dockitty-validate-frontmatter` stop and name the files, the
  address and a fix. Drafts count too, and so do case-only differences, because
  those files overwrite each other on macOS and Windows. Rename or remove all but
  one file in each group.
- **Generated glossary pages take your site's index name, and the build stops in
  three new cases (#129).** Before, the generator always wrote
  `glossary/index.md`. Now it uses `index` when your index names list it, and
  otherwise your first index name: on a site without `index`,
  `glossary/index.md` becomes `glossary/README.md`, and likewise for each context
  folder. If you commit generated pages, commit the rename. The build now stops,
  names the path and writes nothing when a file you wrote or a symbolic link sits
  where a generated page goes, when `glossary/` or a context folder is a symbolic
  link, and when an index name is not a plain file name (one path segment, no
  leading `.`, no surrounding spaces), is empty, or is `log`.
- **On a site that sets `gherkin: { sources }`, ```` ```gherkin ```` fences and
  `::gherkin{…}` lines change meaning (#120).** Before, fences rendered as code
  blocks and a `::gherkin{…}` line printed as text. Now fences render as
  structured scenarios, and `::gherkin{…}` includes a `.feature` file from the
  folders in `includeRoots` (default: `sources`); an include whose file is
  outside them, missing or not a `.feature` file fails the build. Add `raw` to a
  fence (```` ```gherkin raw ````) to keep it as code, or set `fences: false` to
  keep every authored page as it was. An unknown key in the `gherkin` option is
  now a config error instead of being ignored. Sites without the `gherkin` option
  are unaffected.
- **Regenerate your committed feature pages once (#120).** Generated feature
  pages now show quoted step arguments as code (see Changed), so a regenerated
  page differs from the committed one. Run `dockitty-generate-feature-pages`
  once, or the `--check` gate reports the drift.
- **The build stops when no source yields a Gherkin feature and generated pages
  exist (#122).** Before, a source folder that was not checked out, such as an
  uninitialised git submodule, made the build warn and delete every generated
  page. Now the build stops before writing anything and removes nothing. When you
  do want the pages removed, set `gherkin.allowEmpty: true`, or pass
  `--allow-empty` to `dockitty-generate-feature-pages`, for that one build.
  `--check` is unchanged.
- **Move pages you want published out of `_meta/` (#138).** Before, Markdown at
  any depth under a `_meta/` folder, and files named `_meta.md` or `_meta.mdx`,
  were built and linked like any page. Now they are not published, and
  `dockitty-check-links --strict` skips them. The YAML registry files in `_meta/`
  still load, and `dockitty-validate-frontmatter` still checks the Markdown there.
- **`dockitty-new-doc --section` and `dockitty-scaffold` create your first index
  name (#136).** Before, a site with index names `['index', 'README']` could get
  a `README.md`. Now it gets `index.md`. An `--index-basename` value that is not
  one of your index names exits 2.
- **A theme slot name outside the `dk:` set stops the build (#114).** Before, a
  misspelt slot such as `dk:site-heading` in a plain-JavaScript config was
  accepted, and the stock component rendered without a message. Now the config
  fails to load with an error that names the slot and lists the valid names.
  Correct the name. A theme typed as `DocKittyTheme` in TypeScript already caught
  this. See [ADR-0052](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0052-runtime-slot-name-validation.md).
- **`docKittyDocsLoader` rejects a custom `pattern` (#133).** Before, a narrowed
  `pattern` changed which pages were built but not which pages relative links
  could point to, so a `.md` link could be rewritten to a page that was never
  built. Now the loader throws when `pattern` is anything but the default. Leave
  `pattern` unset; to keep a file out of the site, move it out of the docs folder
  or name it `log.md`.
- **Rename any Gherkin file called `index.feature` (#137).** Before, it was
  accepted unless your index names included `index`, and its generated page then
  collided with the folder's landing page. Now the build stops on it whatever
  your index names are.

### Changed

- **The reading column is wider, and all body content uses it (#154).** The
  default `--dk-width-content` goes from `45rem` (720px) to `60rem` (960px), so
  prose, tables, diagrams, code blocks and components share one wider column
  instead of a narrow strip on large screens. The column still stays clear of the
  "On this page" rail and respects `--dk-width-frame`; phones and tablets look as
  before. Prose lines grow from about 92–101 to 123–135 characters. To keep the
  old width, set `:root { --dk-width-content: 45rem; }`. See
  [Theming and chrome](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/architecture/theming.md#reading-width) and
  [ADR-0053](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0053-reading-width.md).
- **Sidebars no longer repeat their own labels, on every site with
  autogenerated groups (#112).** Before, a folder whose only page was its index
  showed as a group holding the same name (glossary contexts read `hr > hr`), and
  a section's index repeated its heading ("Guides > Guides"). Now a nested
  one-page folder shows as that one link, in the folder's place, and a section
  index whose label repeats its heading reads "Overview", unless another page in
  the group already has that label. Top-level sections stay groups, and previous
  and next links keep the page title. "Overview" is English only for now (#161
  tracks translating it).
- **Quoted step arguments render as code, on generated pages and in fences and
  includes alike (#120).** A double-quoted argument such as
  `"spec-kitty init --force"` renders as inline code with its quotes, so the page
  no longer curls the quotes or turns `--` into a dash, and the value copies
  exactly. This applies in data-table and Examples cells too. Text outside quotes
  is still typeset, and a quoted argument is no longer glossary-linked.
- **A broken in-page Gherkin fence or include fails the build (#120).** Before,
  the page built empty. Now a Gherkin syntax error, or an include whose file,
  scenario or tag is not found, stops `astro build` with one
  `[dk-gherkin] <page>:<line>` error listing every broken page, and keeps failing
  until you fix it.
- **A Gherkin folder whose features are all drafts gets a draft hub (#124).**
  Before, it got no hub, so with drafts built (the default) the sidebar asked for
  an index page you could not add. Now the generator writes a hub marked
  `doc_status: draft` with no list, built only when drafts are and linked from no
  published hub. The generated files do not depend on `DK_PUBLISH_DRAFTS`, so
  `--check` agrees in both modes. Such a folder gets one new generated file: run
  the generator once, or `--check` reports it as `added`.
- **A mis-cased `@wip` or `@deprecated` tag warns (#123).** Before, a tag such as
  `@WIP` was published silently as an ordinary page tag. It still is, since the
  status shorthands match exactly as Cucumber tag filters do, but the build now
  asks "did you mean `@wip`?".
- **`dockitty-check-links` checks reference-style link definitions and names a
  bad option (#131).** Before, a dangling `[label]: target` line passed, and an
  unknown option was read as a docs folder that could not be opened. Now the
  definition is reported like an inline link, and an unknown option or the
  `--name=value` form stops the command before scanning, names the option and
  exits 2. The failure summary reads "N link problem(s) in M file(s); F file(s)
  scanned, C reference(s) checked."

### Added

- **Gherkin in any page (#120).** Set `gherkin: true` and a ```` ```gherkin ````
  fence on any docs page renders as a structured scenario: the feature and
  scenarios as headings in the page outline, steps as a list with the keyword in
  bold, data tables and Examples as tables, doc strings as code blocks, and `#`
  comments hidden. A fence may hold a whole feature, scenarios without a
  `Feature:` line, or bare steps. Inside a list, quote or aside the headings stay
  out of "On this page". Slide decks keep fences as code, and generated feature
  pages are left as they are. See
  [ADR-0051](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0051-gherkin-in-any-page.md).
- **Include a `.feature` file from your repository with `::gherkin{src="…"}`
  (#120).** Include the whole file, one scenario with `scenario="<exact name>"`,
  or the scenarios and Examples rows that carry any of `tags="@a @b"` (inherited
  tags count). Each include ends in a source line naming the file, linked with
  `sourceUrlPrefix`. Includes need `gherkin.includeRoots` (or `sources`) and read
  only regular files of at most 1 MiB inside those folders. A page that includes
  a file is re-rendered when the file changes, in a build and in the dev server.
- **New `gherkin` option forms (#120).** `gherkin: true` turns on fences only,
  with no generated pages. The object form gains `fences` (default `true`) and
  `includeRoots`, and `sources` becomes optional: it is what turns on generated
  pages and the `behaviour` section.
- **The agent page payload expands includes (#120).** `/api/pages/<slug>.json`
  has each include as Markdown in place of the directive, and lists them under
  `includes: [{ src, scenario?, tags? }]`.
- **Show each scenario's last test result next to it (#162).** Before, feature
  pages showed what a scenario says but not whether it passed. Now set
  `gherkin.results` to the Cucumber Messages or JSON report your CI writes, and
  every scenario from a `.feature` file, on generated pages and in `::gherkin`
  includes, shows its result after its heading: Passed, Failed, Ambiguous,
  Undefined, Pending, Skipped, Not run or Passed on retry. Outline rows get a
  `Result` column, and each feature a line with the run date and commit. A report
  made from another version of a file shows nothing for it. Produce the report in
  CI rather than committing it; only statuses are published. A missing report
  warns, an unreadable one fails the build. `/api/scenarios.json` carries the
  results too. See [ADR-0055](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0055-gherkin-scenario-results.md).
- **Relative Markdown links between pages work on the built site (#131).**
  Before, `[setup](./setup.md)` linked to a `.md` path that 404s on the live
  site, so authors wrote root-absolute links that break on GitHub. Now a relative
  `.md` or `.mdx` link to a published page becomes that page's address, with your
  `base` applied, and the same link still works on GitHub. A link that does not
  resolve is left as written and reported by `dockitty-assert-no-broken-links`.
  Raw HTML anchors are not rewritten. After renaming a page, restart the dev
  server. See [ADR-0047](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0047-relative-markdown-links.md).
- **`dockitty-check-links --strict` checks links the way the build sees them
  (#131).** Without `--strict`, the check reads files as GitHub does, as in
  0.2.0. With it, a relative `.md` link passes only when the build would turn it
  into a link to a published page. It also reports links to files that are not
  pages (such as `log.md`) or lie outside the docs folder, paths that leave the
  docs folder and come back, malformed `%` escapes, folder links with no index
  page, bare relative links with no extension and, with
  `DK_PUBLISH_DRAFTS=off`, links to drafts. A site built with the toolkit should
  pass `--strict`; without it, the command prints one note suggesting it.
  `--help` lists the options.
- **`gherkin.titles` sets Gherkin hub titles (#125).** It maps a folder, relative
  to its source, to the title of its hub, for names a folder can't spell:
  `titles: { hr: 'HR' }` turns the "Hr" hub and sidebar group into "HR". A key
  that matches no folder warns; malformed keys or titles, or `titles` without
  `sources`, fail the build. `dockitty-generate-feature-pages` takes the same
  setting as a repeatable `--titles <dir>=<title>`.
- **`gherkin.allowEmpty` and `--allow-empty` (#122).** They let the build, and
  `dockitty-generate-feature-pages`, remove the generated pages when no source
  yields a feature. Off by default. See the Breaking entry above and
  [ADR-0048](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0048-generated-page-names-and-empty-sources.md).
- **The consumer guide explains the `diagrams` option (#153).** Before, the guide
  did not mention it, and `diagrams: false` could be read as "draw diagrams in
  the browser"; it means the blocks are shown as code. A new section covers
  turning diagrams on, the build and browser render modes, pinning one with
  `DK_DIAGRAM_BUILD_RENDER` (use `client` in CI without Chromium), and the
  self-hosted server PlantUML needs. No behaviour changes. See
  [Optional: Diagrams](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/guides/consumer-setup.md#optional-diagrams).
- **`--help` on `dockitty-generate-feature-pages`.** It prints the flags and
  exits with status 0.

### Fixed

- **`/api/scenarios.json` now exists whenever Gherkin pages are generated
  (#126).** Before, `llms.txt` pointed agents at `/api/scenarios.json` as soon as
  a generated feature page was published, but the address served a 404 unless
  the site had added `src/pages/api/scenarios.json.ts`. Now the `gherkin`
  integration adds it whenever `gherkin.sources` is set, with your `sourceRoot`
  and `sourceUrlPrefix`, under your `base`. You add nothing; a route file you
  already have is kept. A site that removes the `gherkin` option but keeps its
  generated pages must mount `scenarioIndexRoute()` itself. See
  [ADR-0054](https://github.com/spec-kitty/doc-kitty/blob/main/docs/adr/0054-gherkin-draft-hubs-titles-and-scenario-route.md).
- **Folder index pages are linked at the address the site serves (#134).**
  Before, feeds, `llms.txt`, the agent API, related links, the Hub, the scenario
  index and the on-this-page block listed `guide/index.md` as `/guide/index/`,
  and the root page as `/index/`, addresses the site does not serve. Now they use
  `/guide/` and `/`. If you read the agent API, the `route` field changes for
  those pages.
- **Generated glossary pages work on a site whose only index name is `README`
  (#129).** Before, the hub was served at `/glossary/`, but the toolkit's own
  links pointed at `/glossary/index/`, the Hub layout found no children and the
  sidebar did not treat it as the folder's index. The rename in the Breaking
  entry fixes all three. Sites that list `index` keep their output.
- **Old generated glossary pages are removed on upgrade, when they are the
  generator's own output (#129).** An old hub or context page is deleted only if
  it is identical to the page the generator just wrote. A default-settings site
  whose 0.2.0 build left `glossary/index.md` pages gets them removed silently
  when the glossary source is unchanged. If the source changed, or a page has the
  generator's markers but different content, the old page is kept and the build
  warns: delete it.
- **The sidebar uses a folder's `index.md` to label its group (#138).** Before,
  on a site whose only index name is `README`, the site served `index.md` at the
  folder address, but the sidebar did not use it as the group's label. Now it
  does.
- **`dockitty-check-links --strict` checks only files the build publishes
  (#138).** Before, it also read `log.md`, files in dot-folders and files under
  `_meta`. Now it skips them.
- **A glossary term inside a reference-style link no longer gets a second link
  (#139).** Before, the term in `[the term][ref]`, or in a `[ref]: …`
  definition, could become a link inside the link. Now the glossary leaves both
  alone.
- **The sitemap entry for the site root has one form on a site with a base
  path.** Before, it was written with or without a trailing slash depending on
  the order pages were built in, so two builds of the same tree could differ. Now
  it is always written without the trailing slash.
- **The example's rhetoric section lists its pages in reading order (#112).**
  Introduction, Preamble, then About and license.
- **Repository workflows report clearly instead of failing (#117).** The
  accessibility-baseline workflow no longer fails after pushing regenerated
  baselines: it links the pull request in the run summary, and its
  `target_branch` defaults to `main`. A failed Chromium download no longer fails
  the example build on its own: the browser is cached and the download retried.
  A deploy run now states which commit it published, or that nothing changed.

### Known limitations

- Step text in a fence or an include is not glossary-linked (#113).
- A ```` ```gherkin ```` fence that holds only prose, a table or `Examples:` stops
  the build (mark it `raw`); one that holds only comments stays a code block.
  Steps under a `Feature:` line with no `Scenario:` render as its description,
  with a warning.
- `tags` is an any-of list, not a tag expression: `and`, `or`, `not` and
  parentheses are refused.
- Includes in `.mdx` pages are not expanded in the agent payload.
- Re-rendering pages when an included file changes relies on Astro 5 loader
  internals and is to be re-checked for Astro 7 (#119).

## [0.2.0] — 2026-10-13

**Read this before upgrading: set `DK_PUBLISH_DRAFTS=off` in the build that
deploys your live site.** This release adds that setting. Its default is `on`:
draft pages are built and listed, as in 0.1.1, and are now also marked `noindex`
and left out of site search. A page is a draft when its frontmatter says
`doc_status: draft` **or has no `doc_status` at all**. A deployment that does
not set `off` publishes its drafts as `noindex` pages:

```sh
DK_PUBLISH_DRAFTS=off astro build
```

Before you set `off`, give every live page a status other than `draft`, such as
`doc_status: active`. A page with no `doc_status` counts as a draft, so `off`
would leave it out of the build.

The version is `0.2.0` because the layout, sidebar and redirect-gate changes
below are breaking, and under `0.x` the minor number marks a breaking release.

### 💥 Breaking

Each item is described in full under Changed.

- **Pages with `doc_status: draft` or no `doc_status` are now `noindex` and left
  out of site search.** Give every live page a non-draft status such as
  `doc_status: active` to keep it indexed. With `DK_PUBLISH_DRAFTS=off` those
  pages are not built at all.
- **A theme that sets `dk:site-header` now replaces the stock header.** The slot
  name was already valid in 0.1.1 but did nothing. Now the theme's component
  replaces the header, including search and the theme select, so it has to
  supply them.
- **The redirect-coverage gate has new flags and a new failure.** With drafts
  off it needs `--docs` and `--declared-redirects` to accept an old URL that
  leads to a draft, and it fails on any redirect stub that leads to a missing
  page.
- **Sidebar group labels and order change.** Groups take their index page's
  title and `sidebar.order`.
- **A page with no `h2` or `h3` loses its "On this page" rail.**
- **The page frame is full width by default.** Set `--dk-width-frame` for a
  capped frame.
- **The reading column is narrower between 1152px and 1344px viewports**: 528px
  at 1152px (was 600px) and 656px at 1280px (was 664px).

### Changed

- **Draft pages and pages with no `doc_status` are marked `noindex` and left
  out of site search.** They are still built and listed in the sidebar, as in
  0.1.1. What is new: each carries `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">` and
  has no record in the search index. A site that never set `doc_status` builds
  the same pages as before, and every one of them except the root page is now
  `noindex` and unsearchable. Give a page a status other than `draft` (for
  example `doc_status: active`) to make it indexable and searchable again. The
  sitemap, feeds, `llms.txt` and the agent index never listed drafts and still
  do not. The site's root page is never a draft and never `noindex`.

  The marker follows the page's status, not the setting described under Added:
  a draft is `noindex` whenever it is rendered, also on a site that does not
  load its docs through `docKittyDocsLoader`.
- **This project's example site publishes its Plans section and the footnotes
  showcase.** `/plans/`, the two mission pages and
  `/guides/markua-footnotes-showcase/` were drafts and are now
  `doc_status: active`; `/plans/missions/` is a new
